indicator_name: Obesity rate by body mass index (BMI)

national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the population aged 18 years or over classified as obese according to body mass index (BMI). BMI is calculated using body weight and height, with a BMI value of 30 or higher used to classify obesity.
national_rationale: The indicator provides information on the prevalence of obesity among the population aged 18 years or over in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Monitoring this indicator provides insight into changes in the health and nutritional status of the population over time and contributes to monitoring Sustainable Development Goals related to health and well-being.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator is presented for Bosnia and Herzegovina within the Eurostat `sdg_02_10` dataset. According to Eurostat methodology, the indicator is based on data from the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS) and the Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (SILC). For SILC data referring to 2022, the PH110 variable, relating to body mass index (BMI), is used. Eurostat obtains data for the indicator from data collected through national surveys. The indicator value represents the percentage of the population aged 18 years or over classified as obese, i.e. with a BMI value of 30 or higher. For international comparison, the series published by Eurostat in the `sdg_02_10` dataset is used. At the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Ministry of Civil Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina coordinates activities in the field of health and, in cooperation with the competent health authorities, participates in updating, verifying and processing data for domestic and international reporting. This institutional framework includes cooperation with competent health institutions in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the exchange of data with domestic and international institutions. The collection of data on the health status of the population in Bosnia and Herzegovina faces methodological, logistical and systemic limitations that may affect the availability, quality and comparability of data. Important limitations include possible self-reporting error, limitations or outdatedness of sampling frames, a high non-response rate and long periods between individual survey rounds. These limitations should be taken into account when interpreting indicator values and assessing changes over time.
national_long_objective: No specific quantitative target has been established for this indicator at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Progress is monitored on the basis of changes in the obesity rate using available comparable data, taking into account the methodology and periodicity of the data sources.
eu_indicator_definition: This indicator measures the obesity rate according to body mass index (BMI). BMI is calculated as body weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in metres. People aged 18 years or over are considered obese if their BMI is equal to or greater than 30. The overweight category comprises people with a BMI of 25 or higher and includes the pre-obese and obese categories. The indicator is expressed as a percentage of the population aged 18 years or over.
eu_rationale: The indicator is used to monitor the nutritional and health status of the population in the context of the Sustainable Development Goals. The increasing prevalence of obesity represents one of the challenges related to nutrition, physical activity and population health. The indicator is part of the EU Sustainable Development Goal indicator set and is used to monitor progress in the context of SDGs 2 and 3.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator is based on body mass index (BMI), which is calculated as body weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in metres. According to Eurostat methodology, people aged 18 years or over with a BMI value of 30 or higher are classified as obese.   Data for this indicator are sourced from the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS) and the Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (SILC). EHIS data refer to 2008, 2014 and 2019, while SILC data are available for 2017 and 2022. SILC data for 2017 are used to bridge the gap between EHIS-based data for 2014 and 2019.
eu_long_objective: No specific political quantitative target has been established for this indicator at European Union level. The indicator is used to monitor changes in the obesity rate and progress towards Sustainable Development Goals related to nutrition, health and well-being.
